an5.6:1.1: (1) “Bhikkhus, there is no entering upon the unwholesome so long as faith is securely settled in [cultivating] wholesome qualities.
an5.6:1.2: But when faith has disappeared and lack of faith obsesses one, then there is the entering upon the unwholesome.
an5.6:2.1: (2) “There is no entering upon the unwholesome so long as a sense of moral shame is securely settled in [cultivating] wholesome qualities.
an5.6:2.2: But when a sense of moral shame has disappeared and moral shamelessness obsesses one,
an5.6:2.3: then there is the entering upon the unwholesome.
an5.6:3.1: (3) “There is no entering upon the unwholesome so long as moral dread is securely settled in [cultivating] wholesome qualities.
an5.6:3.2: But when moral dread has disappeared and lack of moral dread obsesses one,
an5.6:3.3: then there is the entering upon the unwholesome.
an5.6:4.1: (4) “There is no entering upon the unwholesome so long as energy is securely settled in [cultivating] wholesome qualities.
an5.6:4.2: But when energy has disappeared and laziness obsesses one, then there is the entering upon the unwholesome.
an5.6:5.1: (5) “There is no entering upon the unwholesome so long as wisdom is securely settled in [cultivating] wholesome qualities.
an5.6:5.2: But when wisdom has disappeared and lack of wisdom obsesses one, then there is the entering upon the unwholesome.”
